description: Master protocol specification governing how AI agents (e.g. Robinhood, Gemini) may submit, approve, execute, and audit market trades on behalf of a principal. This document is the source of truth for the companion files in this folder: mcp-server-config.json, trading-schema.json, agent-policies.json, and audit-config.json.

authentication.description: No credentials may ever be committed to version control. All secrets are injected at runtime via environment variables and referenced here only by placeholder syntax.
rules: Never hardcode API keys, tokens, or secrets in any file under version control.
Secrets must be resolved from the process environment or a secrets manager at process start.
If a required environment variable is missing, the MCP server connection must fail closed (refuse to start) rather than fall back to an unauthenticated or placeholder mode.
Rotate credentials immediately if ever found committed to source control history.

riskPolicy.description: Hard limits enforced on every trade intent prior to execution, regardless of agent autonomy level.

agentAutonomy.description: Defines which trade actions an AI agent may execute without human intervention versus which require human approval.

levels.description: Agent may read market data and portfolio state but cannot submit any orders.
Agent may draft trade intents but every order requires explicit human approval before submission.
Agent may auto-execute trades below a notional threshold and within risk policy; trades above the threshold require human approval.
Agent may auto-execute any trade that passes risk policy validation. Reserved for highly trusted, extensively audited agents.

escalationRules: Any trade exceeding maxPositionSizeUSD always requires human approval, regardless of autonomy level.
Any new/unlisted symbol not present in allowedSymbols always requires human approval.
Any order type other than 'market' or 'limit' (e.g. options, margin) always requires human approval.
Two consecutive rejected trades from the same agent suspend that agent's auto-execute privileges pending human review.

tradeLifecycle.description: Ordered states a trade intent passes through from creation to settlement.

auditAndCompliance.description: Every state transition and risk decision must be logged for compliance and post-trade review. See audit-config.json for the full logging specification.
requirements: Every trade intent must be assigned a unique, immutable trade ID at creation.
Every state transition must emit an audit event including timestamp, actor (agent or human), and reason.
All risk policy evaluations (pass/fail) must be recorded, including which rule was evaluated and the computed values.
Audit logs must be tamper-evident (append-only) and retained per audit-config.json retention policy.
Human approvals/rejections must capture the approver identity and rationale.
